correctness.rationale: The orthogonal basis and beta moments give the explicit kernel. Direct tail integration yields formula (1). Quadratic maximization exhausts all evaluation points and the factored derivative identifies all step maxima, including boundaries. Positive Stieltjes mixtures exhaust bounded monotone inputs; reflection proves the lower bound. Exact algebra and direct quadrature were independently compared by the standalone checker. Finite checks corroborate but are not the universal proof.

originality.rationale: A source/claim/alias search of indexed findings and original mathematical literature did not identify an equivalent exact two-branch sharp envelope or a stronger theorem implying it. Full Kaber paper was materially examined; two directly relevant arXiv full-text introductions and constructions were read. Shape-preserving approximation, asymptotic Gibbs overshoot, and Jacobi spectral convergence rates have logically different quantifiers and operators. Bibliographic coverage cannot be exhaustive, leaving residual risk.
residual_risks: An equivalent result could occur in unindexed or non-digitized literature.
Full text of Xiang (2021) and Davis–Hagelstein (2022) was not read; their abstracts concern different questions but do not definitively rule out incidental finite-degree results.
This work does not establish the number of parameter crossings beyond existence.

value.rationale: The sharp range loss of an unconstrained spectral projector on ordered data is a natural quantitative stability invariant, not determined by general best-approximation rates. The complete two-branch parameter family, all extremizers and a change in worst-case geometry yield useful exact bounds for all symmetric Jacobi weights. No claim of a unique crossing or higher-degree theorem is needed for this value.
